comment: A filter's shortcut closes its own dialog as Escape does. Ctrl+B over the canvas opens Colour Balance through its command, the midtones' Cyan-Red slider is moved, and Ctrl+B into the dialog closes it with the preview gone and the layer as it was. Ctrl+B again opens it. Then the same with a number typed into the slider's field, then from the canvas with the dialog open and the main window holding the keyboard, then with Colour Balance rebound to Ctrl+Alt+K on the Keyboard Shortcuts page, where Ctrl+B leaves the dialog open and Ctrl+Alt+K closes and opens it. The texel at (400, 300) is read before and after each close. Nothing is saved.
01, Ctrl+B over the canvas opens Colour Balance through its command, and the dialog takes the keyboard.
02, the midtones' Cyan-Red slider at 60, the preview on the canvas and the layer unchanged.
03, Ctrl+B into the dialog: it closes as Escape closes it, the preview gone and the layer as it was.
04, Ctrl+B again opens it, on its defaults.
05, the slider at 60 and 33 typed into its number field, which holds the keyboard.
06, Ctrl+B in the number field closes the dialog, the layer as it was.
07, opened again and the slider moved, then a click on the canvas with Pan gives the main window the keyboard.
08, Ctrl+B over the canvas closes the open dialog, the layer as it was.
09, Colour Balance rebound to Ctrl+Alt+K on the Keyboard Shortcuts page.
10, Ctrl+Alt+K opens it and the slider is moved, then Ctrl+B into the dialog leaves it open.
11, Ctrl+Alt+K into the dialog closes it, the layer as it was.
